title: Investigate: Dedicated pool scaling regression and emergency remediation
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Summary:
During a peak traffic window on 2026-02-28 we observed persistent capacity shortfalls from one Dedicated tenant pool that caused elevated 5xx rates and throttled throughput below SLA target for approximately 72 minutes. This ticket coordinates the investigation, immediate remediation steps taken, and the follow-up action plan to prevent recurrence.

Observed behavior (high level):
- Autoscaler failed to provision new capacity for pool 'dp-west-2-42' despite target utilization crossing configured threshold (95%).
- Model variants degraded to lower-throughput fallback, increasing per-request latency and token cost.
- Rolling restarts on a subset of nodes coincided with spike; however restart churn was not the primary limiter.

Immediate mitigation applied by on-call: 
- Temporarily increased pool burst limit and manually injected two spare GPU nodes from cold reserve (rollback planned after stabilization). (Slack thread: #inc-dedicated-8124)
- Enabled emergency routing rule to shift non-critical workloads to a lower-cost but higher-latency backup pool to preserve SLA for priority customers.
- Engaged infra to suspend non-essential background jobs (cache warmers, nightly evals) for the affected region.

Initial root-cause hypotheses under investigation: 
1) Autoscaler evaluation window regression: recent autoscaling change in dedicated-3.4 reduced effective scale headroom by extending aggregation window, delaying scale-up decisions under fast bursts.
2) Scheduler backpressure: coupling between kernel selection probe and node health check caused nodes with transient high KV-cache miss rates to be marked degraded and excluded from routing before replacement capacity came online.
3) Capacity accounting race: allocation service masked free nodes due to a stale cache TTL introduced in release dedicated-3.4.

Investigation plan (owners and deliverables):
- Aisha (assignee): correlate autoscaler logs, scale decision timestamps, and cluster metrics. Deliverable: timeline CSV + annotated Grafana panels. (Target: 2026-03-16)
- Diego (compute infra): verify scheduler behavior and node health transition traces; reproduce node exclusion logic in staging. Deliverable: scheduler trace + repro script. (Target: 2026-03-18)
- Lina (runtime): audit recent kernel selection change PRs for any interactions that increase node startup time. Deliverable: PR links + small benchmark. (Target: 2026-03-17)
- Priya (SRE): confirm allocation cache TTL settings and create a short-lived patch to invalidate caches on scale events. Deliverable: patch + canary rollout plan. (Target: 2026-03-15)

Action items (short-term, assigned):
- AI-1 (Aisha): Emit detailed incident timeline, include autoscaler decision events and capacity delta. Link to working doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/incidents/ENG-8124.
- AI-2 (Priya): Deploy cache invalidation patch to staging and 1 canary, monitor for missed allocations. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated/pull/2048.
- AI-3 (Diego + Lina): Add a quick-fix in scheduler: delay marking node 'unroutable' for 30s if startup < 60s; evaluate risk of transient overcommit.
- AI-4 (Aisha): Update runbook with explicit escalation path for capacity shortfalls and step-by-step emergency routing procedure.

Longer-term proposals (for roadmap discussion):
- Autoscaler policy: add adaptive scale-up aggressiveness that short-circuits aggregation window when utilization growth rate > X%/min.
- Capacity safety buffer: reserve a fractional cold pool per region that can be attached in <2 minutes for P0 incidents.
- Observability: add token-level shed counters and per-tenant scale decision tracing to Console dashboards and alerts.
- Evals: build a synthetic burst test that runs during canary windows to validate scale paths.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- Root cause identified and reproduced in staging.
- One short-term mitigation is merged and can sustain traffic in a targeted canary for 48 hours.
- Runbook updated and teammates briefed (postmortem doc + action list complete).
- Follow-up roadmap tickets created for longer-term fixes.

Links and artifacts:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cluster/dedicated-capacity?orgId=1&from=now-4h&to=now
- Confluence incident page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/incidents/ENG-8124
- Slack incident thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0DED/incident-8124
- GitHub PR (cache patch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated/pull/2048

Notes on trade-offs considered so far:
- Aggressive immediate scale-up reduces outage duration but risks overprovisioning and cost spikes for customers; therefore emergency burst attaches are limited to P0 tenant pools only.
- Easing node unroutable criteria improves availability but may route traffic to under-initialized nodes and increase tail latency; so we prefer short grace period + monitoring over immediate permanent change.

Timeline (quick bullets):
- 2026-02-28 14:12 UTC: First elevated 5xx alerts for dp-west-2-42
- 2026-02-28 14:18 UTC: Autoscaler logged pending decision but did not scale due to aggregation window rule
- 2026-02-28 15:02 UTC: Manual cold-pool attach started (mitigation)
- 2026-02-28 15:30 UTC: Emergency routing turned on; 5xxs reduced
- 2026-02-28 16:24 UTC: Traffic returned to SLA-compliant levels; incident declared mitigated

Postmortem follow-up roadmap (tickets to create after this ticket):
- Dedicated autoscaler: fast-path policy (ENG-8210)
- Allocation cache TTL audit & resilience (ENG-8211)
- Scheduler exclusion grace period review (ENG-8212)
- Synthetic burst tests & canaries (ENG-8213)

This ticket will serve as the coordinating artifact until root cause confirmed and PRs merged. Update the tickets listed in "Postmortem follow-up roadmap" once they are created and link PRs + dashboard panels to this incident in Confluence.
